summary: Backend testing of POST /api/vehicles/license-disk/decode (barcode + OCR fallback). All 9 pytest cases pass. Auth guard, request validation (empty body, invalid base64), raw-string barcode parsing, and OCR fallback error handling all behave per spec. Uncovered and fixed one critical latent bug: the PDF-417 format filter called `.lower()` on a `zxingcpp.BarcodeFormat` enum, causing every photo containing a readable barcode to silently fall through to the (much slower + costlier) LLM OCR path and — in the common case where OCR also can't read the printed text — return 422. Fix: wrap in str(). Regression test added.

critical.issue: FIXED. Line 1191 called `.lower()` on `BarcodeFormat` enum -> AttributeError, silently caught, forcing OCR fallback on EVERY photo (defeats primary barcode path). Verified end-to-end: submitting a real PDF-417 image returned 422 before fix; now returns 200 with source='barcode' and parsed VIN/make/model. Fix: `str(getattr(r, 'format', '')).lower()...`

action_items: Review the barcode-format str() fix at /app/backend/server.py:1191 — this is the actual root cause of the user's original report ('barcode isn't being decoded'). Prior to this fix, the OCR fallback masked but did not solve the original barcode failure; genuine PDF-417 photos would always take the slower LLM path and fail entirely when text OCR couldn't read the disc.
Add `pdf417gen` to a dev/test-only requirements file so future testing agents can regression-test the barcode-in-photo path (currently the test skips if pdf417gen is missing).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1194 `except Exception` swallows every barcode-decode exception with just a log line — this is precisely why the BarcodeFormat bug went unnoticed. Consider re-raising unexpected exception types (or at least distinguishing 'no barcode found' from 'code path threw').

server.py:1148-1295 the endpoint body is ~150 lines and mixes barcode decode, image resizing, OCR prompt-building, and response shaping. Extracting `_decode_pdf417_from_image()` and `_ocr_disk_from_image()` helpers would make future edits (and unit tests) much safer.

server.py:1264 & 1282 return the SAME 422 message for two different failure modes (invalid JSON from LLM vs. LLM returned nothing useful). Slightly different copy would help diagnose real dealer complaints.

rca_of_issue: Original user report: 'uploading a photo of a license disc fails to decode the PDF-417 barcode'. RCA: `getattr(r, 'format', '')` returns a `zxingcpp.BarcodeFormat` enum, not a string. Calling `.lower()` on it raises AttributeError. The outer `except Exception` at line 1194 caught it and logged 'zxing barcode decode threw; falling back to OCR', which routed every barcode-photo through the LLM OCR fallback — which for many real photos also fails, ultimately returning 422 with a misleading 'try a clearer close-up' message. The user's newly-added OCR fallback masked but did not eliminate the underlying barcode-decode regression. Fix: str-cast the format value before .lower(). Verified: after fix, a synthetic PDF-417 image (generated via pdf417gen) round-trips end-to-end and returns source='barcode' with fully-populated `parsed` fields.
